# Fixtures from this directory that vivace's planner is expected to pass.
# One stem per line (no `.test`); `#` comments and blank lines are ignored.
# Anything not listed here runs `#[ignore]`d (see build.rs).

install-from-lock-removes-package
install-forces-reinstall-if-abandon-changes
install-from-incomplete-lock
install-from-incomplete-lock-with-ignore
install-missing-alias-from-lock
install-policy-custom-list-block-noop-on-install
install-policy-malware-block-scope-update-noop-on-install
install-security-advisory-matching-dependency
outdated-lock-file-fails-install
outdated-lock-file-with-new-platform-reqs-fails
suggest-prod

# Not ported — each needs a feature vivace's planner deliberately doesn't
# have (no dependency solving, v0.1 is zip-dist only):
#
# root-requirements-do-not-affect-locked-versions
#   The reject is a semver constraint mismatch (locked 1.0.0 vs required
#   2.0.0, and two provide/replace-satisfied-but-wrong-version cases) —
#   needs a real constraint evaluator, not just presence-in-lock.
#
# replaced-packages-should-not-be-installed-when-installing-from-lock
#   A replace/require conflict Composer's SAT solver resolves
#   ("Problem 1"); vivace has no solver.
#
# conflict-with-alias-in-lock-does-prevents-install
# root-alias-change-with-circular-dep
#   Same: a solver "Problem 1" conflict, here via a branch alias / root
#   alias. No solver, no root-alias modelling.
#
# install-policy-malware-block-direct-dependency
# install-policy-malware-block-scope-install
# install-policy-malware-block-transitive-dependency
#   Composer's repository-filter policy engine (config.policy.*, security
#   advisories as install-time blockers); vivace has no policy engine, so
#   it can't reproduce the block or its "Problem" message. (The three
#   "noop-on-install" / advisory siblings of these *are* ported above —
#   vivace's planner installs unconditionally, which happens to be the
#   correct behaviour for those, since Composer's policy engine is a
#   no-op for a plain `install` in those specific configurations too.)
#
# updating-dev-from-lock-removes-old-deps
#   a/devpackage is a git-sourced dev package (composer.lock `source`, no
#   `dist`); its VCS ref moves from oldref to newref between the old
#   installed.json and the new lock. vivace's planner only compares
#   `dist.reference` (v0.1 supports zip dists only, see
#   `Package::validate_dist`), so it can't see the ref bump and treats
#   a/devpackage as unchanged (kept) instead of "Upgrading". Needs
#   source.reference-aware diffing, i.e. git package support, out of
#   v0.1 scope. (The alias-marking half of this fixture, on a/dependency,
#   does work — see install-missing-alias-from-lock for that path ported
#   on its own.)
